# The off-socket adapter cannot reach an App Worker in a second browser context

## Context

#20587 brings four window specs back into the engine tier off-socket. Two stay `LOCAL_ONLY` for a cause measured on 2026-11-08. It differs from the reload #20587 assumed:
- `workstation/WorkstationResetSurvivesReloadNL.spec.mjs` (2 arms)
- `workstation/WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL.spec.mjs`

Both cold-boot the Workstation in a **second browser context** (`neuralLink.newContext()` plus `newPage()`), then bind it with `neuralLink.connectToApp(<App Worker id>)`. Off-socket, that call fails after 30 s: "the page's App Worker (dedicated, or its own SharedWorker) did not initialize Neo.ai.Client within 30000 ms." Over the Bridge it passes, because the Bridge resolves the id across every connected App Worker.

## The Problem

The off-socket fixture (`runDedicatedWorkerNeuralLink`) binds only the fixture's own `page`: that page's dedicated App Worker, or its own SharedWorker through `attachPageSharedAppWorker({page})`. An id naming another context's App Worker can never match. `connectToApp` keeps polling the fixture page, whose context `WorkstationResetSurvivesReloadNL` has already closed after seeding.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/dedicatedWorkerNeuralLink.mjs`, `connectToApp(target)`: a `WORKER_ID` target only filters the fixture page's own candidate (`readyId !== target`).
- `test/playwright/sharedWorkerAppWorker.mjs`: `attachPageSharedAppWorker` finds a page's own SharedWorker by that page's `browserContextId` and the App Worker URL its main thread loads.
- After #20587, the fixture releases a held SharedWorker session in two cases, because a held session keeps the worker alive past its last client: before its page's own document navigates, and when the context's last window closes. A binding to another context's page needs the same two hooks on that page.
- `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs`: the `LOCAL_ONLY` entry this ticket owns. `test/playwright/externalBrainSelection.mjs`: `ADAPTER_ELIGIBLE_SPECS`.

## The Fix

`connectToApp(<App Worker id>)` binds the page whose App Worker reports that id, in any context the browser holds:
- search `browser.contexts()` → `pages()`, reading each page's id through `Neo.worker.App.getWorkerId()`;
- prefer a page without an `opener()`, so a popup never becomes the bound page.

It then serves that page exactly as the fixture page: its dedicated worker, or its SharedWorker through `attachPageSharedAppWorker`, with both release hooks registered on it. The id is a UUID, so the match is exact, and the adapter still never searches by app name.

Once green, each spec moves into `ADAPTER_ELIGIBLE_SPECS` and `RUN_PATHS`, with a duration taken from a hosted log.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `WorkstationResetSurvivesReloadNL` and `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL` pass off-socket locally. Red first: both fail on the base.
- [ ] Both pass on two hosted engine-tier runs and leave `LOCAL_ONLY`. A spec that cannot keeps an entry stating its measured cause.
- [ ] The id binding has a unit arm, in `test/playwright/unit/test/sharedWorkerAppWorker.spec.mjs` or `dedicatedWorkerNeuralLink.spec.mjs`, that fails without it.

## Out of Scope

- Binding by app name across contexts. The adapter addresses a captured worker, never a name.
- The WebSocket Bridge, and the Bridge- and Brain-service classes of `LOCAL_ONLY`.

## Related

- #20587: the re-boot, last-window and window-topology fixes this extends.
- #20451 and PR #20584: the off-socket tier and `LOCAL_ONLY`.

* fix(test): the off-socket adapter releases a held SharedWorker session before its page re-boots (#20587)

A CDP session attached to the App SharedWorker keeps it alive past its last
client. A page that re-booted while the adapter held it connected to that
survivor, whose Data, VDom and Canvas siblings had started fresh, and never
finished booting (a four-arm probe: holding the session fails, detaching before
the navigation passes, the writer pair is irrelevant). A worker kept alive after
its last window closed never answers again either, which hung the fixture's
teardown.

- dedicatedWorkerNeuralLink: a document request of the bound page waits until the
  session is released; the next call attaches the App Worker the new document
  started; the context's last window closing releases it too. `appWorker` holds
  dedicated workers only.
- sharedWorkerAppWorker: a closed handle rejects every later call at once.
- get_window_topology hands rects over as the wire's JSON (Neo.util.Rectangle is
  a DOMRect, whose x / y CDP's returnByValue drops), and a window operation on a
  window the topology does not hold is refused before the App Worker sees it, as
  the Bridge's resolveWindowTarget refuses it.

DockSplitterZoneIdNL, WorkstationFiveBeatNL, EmailMultiWindowNL and WindowOps
pass off-socket and join the engine tier. WorkstationResetSurvivesReloadNL and
WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL bind a second browser context by worker id, which the
adapter cannot reach; they stay LOCAL_ONLY under #20614.
